_comment: 🧩️ This owner's contribution. 🎚️config carries three typed mutation vocabularies, all mounted by the plugin host from direct semantic leaves: opening preferences (set-default-app, clear-default-app), merge policy (change-merge-policy), and identity (sign-in, sign-out). Each vocabulary is claimed by exactly one exhaustive case under 🔌️plugin/🖥️host/🧪️tests, and every kind in every vocabulary carries a committed (before, mutation, after, diff, outcome) specification vector beside its own leaf.

noOracleDecisions.rationale:
`os.config.opening` is this operating system's own preference record — a list of `(artifact dialect, role) -> app` pins, where the dialect is a semio `ArtifactDialect` triple and the app is a semio `AppRef`. There is no third-party implementation of it and no third party could hold an opinion about it: what is under test is that a pin is an UPSERT keyed on `(dialect, role)` rather than an append, that clearing a pin nobody set is a warned no-op rather than an error, and that `set` and `clear` are exact inverses of each other on that key — statements about this repository's own preference semantics, not about JSON or key-value storage. Confidence comes instead from the two committed, independently handcrafted `(before, mutation, after, outcome)` specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<slug>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/`, each already unit-tested inside the facet itself, re-exercised end to end through `apply_opening_config_mutation_reporting`; and from the inverse law as a metamorphic property. Both vectors run against the same two-pin document — a cad viewer pin and a cad editor pin — which is what lets each kind be held to the claim that it touches ONE pin and leaves its sibling alone.

[C2 2026-09-02] Narrowed `capabilities` to remove 'os-config-opening-1-mutate': a mutation manifest already requires an external-oracle discharge for this capability (tracked honestly as `missing-external-oracle`), so a no-oracle decision claiming the same capability made that gap invisible to `no-oracle-covers-mutation` without discharging it. The rationale above is kept verbatim as the record of what was actually investigated; only the claim is withdrawn. See .🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️09/☀️02/SEPARATE-ARTIFACT-STANDARD-SUBSET-IMPLEMENTATIONS-AND-FIXTURE-TEST-EVERY-MUTATION/📓️c2-native-artifact-oracles.md.

`os.config.merge-policy` is repository-owned authority configuration with no independent third-party implementation: what is under test is that a policy change replaces the WHOLE single-field record, that asking for the policy already active is a warned no-op which hands the unchanged record back rather than resetting it to the facet default, and that the undo carries the policy read off the pre-mutation record. Those are statements about this repository's own authority semantics, not about JSON or enums. Confidence comes instead from the committed, independently handcrafted `tightens-the-authority-to-vigilant` specification vector under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/🛡️change-merge-policy/🧪️tests/`, already unit-tested inside the facet itself and re-exercised end to end through `apply_merge_policy_config_mutation_reporting`; and from the inverse law as a metamorphic property.

The rationale above is kept verbatim as the record of what was actually investigated; only the claim is withdrawn. See .🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️09/☀️02/SEPARATE-ARTIFACT-STANDARD-SUBSET-IMPLEMENTATIONS-AND-FIXTURE-TEST-EVERY-MUTATION/📓️c2-native-artifact-oracles.md.

`os.config.identity` is repository-owned session configuration with no independent third-party implementation. `IdentitySetting` is `Option<Identity>` and nothing else, so a session is established whole or absent whole and the vocabulary closes at two kinds. What is under test is that both kinds read their undo off the PRE-MUTATION record rather than off their own payload — replacing one session must undo to the prior session and not to a sign-out, and clearing an already-cleared record must offer no undo step at all rather than inventing an account. Confidence comes from the two committed, independently handcrafted specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<slug>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/`, each already unit-tested inside its own leaf and re-exercised end to end through `apply_identity_config_mutation_reporting`; from the inverse law as a metamorphic property; and from the Rust and TypeScript leaves agreeing on the shared camel-case JSON projection.
